# Comparative Evaluation

This chapter brings together the results from all Stage 2 models - classical embeddings
(Word2Vec, FastText) and fine-tuned compact LLMs (TinyLlama 1.1B, Gemma 2 2B) - and
evaluates them on a common basis across three dimensions: classification performance,
computational cost, and interpretability.

## A Note on Label Quality

All models are evaluated against sentiment labels derived from
`cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest`, a RoBERTa model trained on Twitter data.
Our corpus consists of long-form AI media articles - a substantially different domain.
The F1 scores therefore reflect agreement with the labelling model rather than true sentiment
accuracy, which places a practical ceiling on all results. This ceiling appears to be around
0.76 Macro-F1, as no model exceeded this threshold regardless of size or architecture.

## Overall Results

```{python}
#| label: summary-table
#| echo: true

import pandas as pd

summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model": ["Word2Vec + LR", "FastText + LR",
    "TinyLlama 1.1B", "Gemma 2 2B"],
    "Type": ["Classical", "Classical", "Fine-tuned LLM", "Fine-tuned LLM"],
    "Macro-F1": [0.752, 0.745, 0.757, 0.761],
    "Training Time": ["~2 min", "~2 min", "~28 min", "~66 min"],
    "Hardware": ["CPU (local)", "CPU (local)", "A100 (cloud)", "A100 (cloud)"],
    "CO2 (g)": ["~0.2", "~0.2", "~65", "~125"],
})

summary["Macro-F1"] = summary["Macro-F1"].map("{:.3f}".format)

styled = (
    summary.style
    .set_properties(**{"text-align": "center"})
    .set_table_styles([
        {"selector": "th", "props": [("text-align", "center"),
        ("background-color", "#f0f0f0")]}
    ])
)
styled
```

## Key Findings

**Classical embeddings are surprisingly competitive.** Word2Vec achieves 0.752 Macro-F1 - only
0.009 below the best model (Gemma 2 2B, 0.761) - while training in 2 minutes on a laptop CPU
with a CO2 footprint 625 times smaller than Gemma 2. For this specific task and dataset,
classical methods deliver near-equivalent performance at a fraction of the cost.

**Model size yields diminishing returns.** Doubling the parameter count from TinyLlama (1.1B)
to Gemma 2 (2B) improved Macro-F1 by only 0.004. The marginal gain does not justify the
2.4x increase in training time and energy consumption.

**All models struggle equally with minority classes.** Negative and positive sentiment both
score around F1 = 0.72 across all approaches, while neutral consistently scores ~0.83.
This pattern reflects the class imbalance in the dataset (neutral = 61%, positive = 24%,
negative = 15%) rather than model-specific weaknesses.

**The label quality ceiling matters.** Since sentiment labels were generated by a Twitter-trained
RoBERTa model applied to long-form journalism, the practical upper bound for any model on this
task is well below 1.0. The narrow spread of results (0.745–0.761) across very different
architectures suggests all models are approaching this ceiling.

## Conclusion

For AI trend detection in media texts, classical Word2Vec embeddings combined with logistic regression offer the best cost-performance ratio. Fine-tuned LLMs provide marginal improvements at substantially higher computational cost and carbon footprint. The choice between approaches should be guided by the deployment context: if inference speed, energy efficiency, and
interpretability matter, classical models are the pragmatic choice. If marginal accuracy gains justify GPU infrastructure, compact fine-tuned LLMs are a viable alternative.

## Insight Extraction: What Do the Embeddings Reveal About AI Trends?

Beyond classification performance, we use the best-performing classical model (Word2Vec) to examine the thematic structure of AI discourse. By projecting document embeddings into 2D with UMAP and colouring by the topic labels derived in Stage 1, we can directly inspect how topics cluster in the learned embedding space - and what this reveals about the organisation of AI
media coverage.

```{python}
#| label: insight-extraction
#| echo: true

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import umap
from pathlib import Path
from gensim.models import Word2Vec

_cwd = Path.cwd()
REPO_ROOT  = _cwd if (_cwd / "data").exists() else _cwd.parents[1]
STAGE2_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data/processed/stage2"

# Load data and model
train = pd.read_parquet(STAGE2_DIR / "train.parquet")
test  = pd.read_parquet(STAGE2_DIR / "test.parquet")
train["tokens"] = train["tokens"].apply(eval)
test["tokens"]  = test["tokens"].apply(eval)

w2v_model = Word2Vec.load(str(STAGE2_DIR / "word2vec.model"))

def mean_pooling(tokens, model):
    vectors = [model.wv[t] for t in tokens if t in model.wv]
    return np.mean(vectors, axis=0) if vectors else np.zeros(model.vector_size)

# Combine train and test for a fuller picture
all_df = pd.concat([train, test], ignore_index=True)
all_df = all_df.dropna(subset=["topic_label"]).reset_index(drop=True)
X_all  = np.array([mean_pooling(t, w2v_model) for t in all_df["tokens"]])

# UMAP projection
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_components=2, random_state=42, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1)
proj    = reducer.fit_transform(X_all)

# Plot coloured by topic
topics  = all_df["topic_label"].tolist()
unique_topics = sorted(set(topics))
palette = plt.cm.get_cmap("tab10", len(unique_topics))
color_map = {t: palette(i) for i, t in enumerate(unique_topics)}
colors  = [color_map[t] for t in topics]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))
for topic in unique_topics:
    mask = [t == topic for t in topics]
    ax.scatter(proj[mask, 0], proj[mask, 1],
               c=[color_map[topic]], s=3, alpha=0.4, label=topic)

ax.legend(markerscale=4, fontsize=8, loc="upper right",
          framealpha=0.8, title="Topic")
ax.set_title("Word2Vec Document Embeddings - UMAP projection coloured by Topic (Stage 1 labels)")
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The projection reveals a clear thematic organisation of AI media discourse that goes beyond what classification metrics can capture. **Search, SEO & Marketing** (grey) forms two distinct isolated clusters outside the main body, reflecting its highly domain-specific vocabulary around search engines and digital marketing. **Stocks & Market Ratings** (yellow-green) separates cleanly to the right, and **Quantum Computing** (pink) clusters at the bottom right of the main body - both topics carry specialised terminology with little overlap with general AI coverage. **Consumer Tech** (red) appears as a compact cluster above the main body, while **Energy, Power & Robotics** (purple) sits at the upper left periphery. At the core, **AI News & Tech (General)** dominates the dense centre, with **ML Models & Training Data** heavily overlapping - consistent with the difficulty all models had separating these two classes in classification.

Crucially, this structure was learned entirely from word co-occurrence statistics, without any topic supervision. The fact that Word2Vec recovers the broad organisation of AI discourse unsupervised demonstrates that classical embeddings trained on domain-specific text capture
genuine thematic structure - making them a practical tool for tracking how AI topics relate and evolve over time.
